input.brief: Pillow — the friendly fork of the Python Imaging Library: open, transform and save images in Python

direction.name: One motif
direction.idea: Take one shape from the subject and let it run the whole system. A drilling tool's octagonal cross-section becomes the buttons, the image masks and the loader. A two-account money app becomes two circles that recur as icon, inline dot and section colour. A café's striped awning becomes every band on the page. Look at the product, the logo, the object or the word in the headline and find the simplest geometry in it (a circle, an arc, a chamfer, a stripe, a notch, a ring). Then use only that shape, at three or four very different scales, everywhere a designer would normally reach for a generic rounded rectangle.
direction.composition: Hero: the motif appears once at enormous scale as a flat filled shape, cropped by the viewport (a circle 120vh across entering from the right, a chamfered block filling the lower half), with a short headline at 6–8vw and one supporting sentence set on the remaining ground, left-aligned on a shared margin. Through the page the motif returns as: the mask for every photograph (via `clip-path` or `border-radius` made from the same geometry), the shape of the primary button, the bullet beside list items at text size, and one full-width band that separates the two halves of the page. Sections use simple two-column or single-column layouts so the shape is the only thing with character.
direction.typography: A clean geometric or grotesk face that echoes the shape (round bowls for circles, squared terminals for chamfers). Medium weight; headings 6–8vw in the hero and 3–4vw after.
direction.colour: The motif carries the accent colour at large scale, flat. Everything else is ground and ink. A second motif colour is allowed only if the subject has a real pair (two accounts, two modes).
direction.imagery: Photographs appear inside the motif's shape. If there is product interface to show, it sits on a flat colour stage shaped by the motif. Draw the shape with CSS or a simple inline SVG path; do not draw illustrations.
direction.richness: One shape at many sizes. The giant cropped shape gives the hero mass and colour without a single image.
direction.pitfalls: One motif means one. A circle here, a hexagon there and a blob behind is the generated look this replaces. The motif must come from the subject and you must be able to say from where in one clause.

hero.name: Giant cropped shape
hero.blueprint: A plain ground with one flat shape at enormous scale. The shape is the simplest geometry found in the subject (a circle, a ring segment, a chamfered block, an arch), drawn in CSS or as a single inline SVG path and filled with the accent colour. It is about 120vh across and enters from the right, centred near 78% of the width and 55% of the height, so the top, right and bottom edges of the viewport crop it and its left boundary reaches column 7. If the subject has a true pair (two accounts, two modes), a second shape in a second flat colour overlaps the first by a quarter with `mix-blend-mode: multiply`. The headline sits on the bare ground on columns 1–6, vertically centred, flush left at 8% from the left edge: two lines at clamp(64px, 6.4vw, 100px), heavy weight, tracking -0.03em. Beneath it comes one supporting sentence at 19px, then the single action as a solid button cut to the same shape. A bold wordmark sits top-left at 32px; up to three text links sit top-right in the ground colour.
hero.mobile: The shape moves to the bottom: 130vw across, centred horizontally, its top at 56svh, cropped by the left, right and bottom edges. The headline sits above it at 11.5vw on two lines at a 16px margin, starting 15% down, with the sentence at 16px and the motif-shaped button beneath. Wordmark top-left; the links collapse to one word top-right.
hero.headline: Two lines of two or three words each, up to about 12 characters per line at 6.4vw.

type.note: A geometric sans in a light weight at large size, soft and exact at once, with its text cut underneath. Suits consumer apps, utilities and developer tools that want to feel calm and modern.

palette.name: Bottle green, gold
palette.note: Bottle green covers the page and warm gold sets all the type, with panels one step lighter than the ground. The button is solid gold with green text, and photographs are kept dark and warm so the pair is not disturbed.

motion.name: Shutter image
motion.description: The one hero or showcase image opens from an edge with a clip-path over about 1.1 seconds while the picture inside settles from 1.12 scale to rest. Use it once, on the image that matters most; later images simply are there. Recipe: 'Image shutter' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: Close-ups on a board
sections.blueprint: A board of filled tiles, each a macro view of one small part of the interface. A 12-column grid with 8px gaps, 104px rows and 10px outer margins, no empty cells, no outlines. Eight tiles in four sizes: 6×4, 6×2, 3×4 and 3×2 (columns × rows). Each tile is a flat palette colour with overflow: hidden and holds one real element, built in em and enlarged to 300–400% through the font-size of its data-ui root: a toggle, a pair of key caps, a status word on its block, one figure from a readout, a slider thumb on its track, three stacked initials discs. The element is pushed off-centre so two of the tile's edges crop it. Bottom-left in every tile, 20px in: the capability's name at 18px medium and one line at 15px. One 6×2 tile holds only the heading, two to four words at clamp(36px, 4vw, 60px), top-left.
sections.mobile: Two columns, 6px gaps, rows of 28vw. Large tiles span both columns and three rows; the rest are one column by two rows. The heading tile leads at full width, two rows tall, type at 9vw. Enlarged elements keep their scale and are cropped harder; captions stay bottom-left at 16px and 14px.

sections.name: One control, blown up
sections.blueprint: A flat saturated field, full-bleed and 92svh tall, holds one working control from the product: the toggle, slider, segmented switch or record button the whole product turns on. Build it at true proportions with every dimension in em, mark its root data-ui, then raise that root's font-size until the control stands about 46vh tall. Anchor it right of centre so the section's right and bottom edges crop about a fifth of it (overflow: hidden on the section). It keeps its real label and value, now at poster size, and it works: operating it swaps the field between two palette colours and changes one word of the heading. The heading, two to four words at clamp(28px, 2.6vw, 40px), sits top-left on the page margin with one sentence at 17px beneath it. The lower-left third of the field stays empty.
sections.mobile: The field is 86svh. Heading and sentence sit top-left at 26px and 16px. The control is enlarged to about 130vw wide and anchored bottom-left, so the right edge crops its far end while its thumb or active segment stays within reach. It still works and still swaps the field colour.

sections.name: Many into one
sections.blueprint: A diagram drawn with one repeated shape instead of arrows. The heading (two to four words on two lines at clamp(36px, 4vw, 60px)) and a short paragraph at 17px sit in columns 1–4. Beneath, a wide inline SVG spans columns 1–12 at about 4.5:1. It is built from 120–160 small filled squares (or the page's own motif), each 10–14px. In the left third they are scattered loosely in two pale tones. In the middle third they are pulled into a tight horizontal ribbon three squares high. In the right third they fan out again into neat, evenly spaced rows in the accent colour. The eye reads disorder, compression, order, from left to right. Under the diagram, three text columns aligned to its thirds: a bold one-word name at 20px and two lines at 16px each; the words carry the sequence ('Gather', 'Reduce', 'Release'). No connecting marks.
sections.mobile: The diagram turns to run top to bottom: a 3:4 SVG with the scatter at the top, the ribbon as a vertical band in the middle and the ordered rows at the bottom. The three names and their text sit to its right in a 38vw column, each level with its zone.

sections.name: Line-up at one type size
sections.blueprint: A full-bleed flat section. The programme is a four-column table spanning the full width between 24px margins, with every cell at one size, clamp(20px, 2.1vw, 30px), one weight, no bold: the act or session flush left, the format starting at 33%, the room or stage at 66%, and the time range right-aligned at the far edge with tabular figures. Rows are 1.5em tall and separated by nothing but that leading; the fixed column starts do the organising. Day or part headings are a single line at the same size in the accent ink with 72px above and 20px below, and may be `position: sticky; top: 0` on a strip of the section's ground colour so the current day stays in view. Breaks and changeovers are rows set in capitals in the soft ink. There is no other heading. Comfortably holds 12–40 rows; with fewer than eight, raise the size to 3vw.
sections.mobile: Each entry becomes two lines: the act at 22px on the first, then format, room and time on one line at 14px in the soft ink with the time right-aligned. 18px between entries. Day headings stay sticky at the top on the ground colour.

sections.name: Inset panel, shaped portrait
sections.blueprint: A deep-toned panel inset 20px from the page edges with a 12px radius, about 110svh tall, `overflow: hidden`. Left half: a two-line statement of four to seven words at clamp(40px, 4.4vw, 64px) in a pale ink, top-left with 56px padding; it is the heading and has nothing above it. Below it a photograph of the person or the workshop, masked with `clip-path` or an SVG `mask` to one bold shape taken from the subject (a four-lobed flower, a circle, an arch, a chamfered block), 38vw across, positioned so the panel's bottom edge crops its lowest fifth. Right side, starting at 63% of the width and 56px from the top: two text blocks 300px wide and 64px apart, each a subhead at 22px over a four-line paragraph at 15px; then one solid button in the accent colour. Between the statement and the text blocks the panel is empty. One photograph only.
sections.mobile: The panel is inset 10px and stacks: the statement at 8.5vw, then the two text blocks at full width, the button, and last the shaped photograph at 86vw across, centred and cropped by the panel's bottom edge by a quarter of its height.

sections.name: Names as one sentence
sections.blueprint: Client, press or partner names are written out as one run-on sentence and set large: clamp(40px, 5vw, 76px), leading 1.0, flush left across all twelve columns, wrapping naturally over five to seven lines. Names are separated by commas and the list ends with a full stop. All names are set in a dimmed ink (still at least 3:1 against the ground), so the block reads as texture; one name at a time is lit in the full ink, and the lit name moves through the list every two seconds (a class toggled by a short script, with a 400ms colour transition). The sentence opens with two or three plain words in the full ink that act as the heading: the phrase that introduces the names. Nothing else is in the section: no logos, no columns, and 120px of space above and below.
sections.mobile: The same sentence at 9vw, wrapping over ten to fourteen lines; cut the list to the twelve strongest names so it stays within one and a half screens. The lit name still cycles. Margins are 20px and there are no other elements.

sections.name: Accordion of filled tiles
sections.blueprint: A two-part row. Columns 1–4 hold the heading, two to four words at about 4vw, `position: sticky; top: 96px` so it stays while the list scrolls past. Columns 5–12 hold the accordion: each question is a filled tile one step from the page ground, with 8px between tiles, no border and the page's one radius (or its motif's corner). A closed tile is 72px tall with the question at 20px medium on the left, 24px padding, and on the right a plus sign drawn from two 3px bars 16px long. The open tile switches to the accent colour with its assigned ink, the plus becomes a minus by rotating one bar, and the answer appears at 17px, no wider than 52ch. Build each tile as `<details>` with a shared `name` so one opens at a time. Six to nine tiles.
sections.mobile: The heading sits above at 9vw, not sticky. Tiles run full width with 6px gaps, questions at 18px wrapping to two lines, closed height at least 64px. The open tile keeps the accent colour, and answers are set at 16px with 20px padding.

sections.name: First step, already open
sections.blueprint: The page ends with the product's first screen already open. A full-bleed field in the accent colour, 90svh tall. Right, in columns 7–11, vertically centred: the product's own create dialog at true size, 440px wide, root marked data-ui, with its real title ('Name your workspace'), one text field holding an editable, believable example, one two-option segmented choice and its primary button. Inside the fragment the product's conventions apply, including the shadow its dialog normally casts. The field accepts typing, the choice switches, and the primary button is the page's only action: it carries the typed value into sign-up. Left, in columns 1–5, anchored to the bottom with 40px margins: the closing line, two to four words at clamp(56px, 7vw, 112px), leading 0.92, on two lines, and under it one sentence at 17px saying what happens after the button. The upper-left stays empty.
sections.mobile: The closing line leads at 13vw on two lines, top-left, with its sentence beneath at 16px. The dialog follows at full width inside 16px margins, at true size, its primary button 52px tall and full width. The field is at least 84svh; the dialog sits in its lower half.

sections.name: The mark, built large
sections.blueprint: On a flat colour field, the brand closes the page as a construction rather than as set type. Across the full content width and about 34svh tall, the wordmark is built from blocks: each letter is knocked out of its own solid rectangle in a palette colour, the rectangles differ in height (60–100% of the band) and butt together with 4px gaps, bottoms on one line. Where the project has a simple geometric mark or motif, enlarge that instead, drawn as inline SVG from flat rectangles, circles and quarter-arcs with the same 4px gaps. Below, 56px lower: four columns of plain links at 15px across columns 1–8, and two addresses or contact lines in columns 9–12. A last row carries the copyright at the left and one small filled button at the right. Space and the block construction do all the separating.
sections.mobile: The block wordmark spans the full width at about 22svh tall; a long name breaks into two rows of blocks. Link columns go two across at 15px, contact lines beneath at full width, then copyright and the small button on one row.

references.name: Superlocal 2026
references.idea: Everything is a circle: a dot-matrix logotype whose dots become floating photo circles and glowing orbs across a grey-to-orange field.
references.hero: Mid-grey field with a faint dot grid (one dot every 33px) that fades through the lower half into saturated orange at the bottom edge. The captured first paint contains one element: a 270×80px logotype dead centre, built from black ellipses of varying size, its letters progressively compressed to the right. No nav or text yet. After loading, a cluster of four small pills (one black, three white) appears top-centre; the logo turns white inside a 330px ring of about fifty tiny circles — round photo crops, glowing orbs, coins; and the bottom edge carries the event name left and dates right in an outlined dot-matrix face 40px tall.
references.type: Display text is an outlined dot-matrix face drawn on canvas, about 40px caps, modules flickering. All other text is one tight bold grotesk ('fontSans') from 12 to 24px with negative tracking. The logotype is built from ellipses on the same matrix.
references.colour: #bcbcbc #ff641e #1a1302 #ffb740 #c13bff #ffffff — Every screen repeats a vertical fade from flat grey to hot orange. Orbs add magenta-violet cores; the footer swaps to a soft yellow glow. Text is near-black, nav pills black and white.
references.imagery: Event photographs cropped to circles from 60 to 240px, floating without a grid alongside hard-edged radial-gradient orbs and coin images; some pairs overlap. The logo and footer art are generated dot matrices.
references.layout: No visible grid: circles drift across each screen while text locks to the bottom corners (statement bottom-left, description bottom-right). A four-pill nav stays top-centre. The footer resolves into three text columns over a screen-filling dot-matrix glow.

sections.description: No grid. Circular photo crops between 60 and 240px across float over the grey-to-orange field, a few overlapping in pairs. A flat radial orb (orange rim, magenta-violet core, about 160px) sits among them and others are cut by the viewport edges. The pill nav stays top-centre; nothing else is fixed.

Bottom-left: a small bold date line, then a two-line statement in the outlined dot-matrix face at about 36px, some modules lit orange mid-animation. Bottom-right: a two-line 12px bold description. Above them three photo circles (190px portrait near centre, poster collage left, stage shot right) and a large orb top-right.

Grey field with a huge soft yellow radial glow. The dot-matrix logo is enlarged to fill the screen, its ellipses knocked out of the yellow in grey. On top: three columns of bold 18px text (contact message and email left, press list centre, socials right), a tiny credits list, and a bottom line with dates, year and city in the same three columns.

steal: Build the logotype from a dot matrix of ellipses of varying size, then reuse the same matrix at screen-filling scale as the footer background.
Crop every photo to a circle at wildly different diameters and let them float with coloured orbs instead of sitting in a gallery grid.
Fade each screen from flat grey into one saturated colour at its bottom edge so the viewport itself carries the brand colour.

references.name: Billow
references.idea: A conventional product page softened by a cloud motif: the logo's cloud silhouette is blown up and blurred into a blue stage for the app.
references.hero: Centred stack on near-white. Nav inside a 1230px container: cloud logo left, four links centred, outline Log in and navy pill right. A small outlined pill badge, then a two-line title-case serif headline at 6.4vw with -0.05em tracking in deep navy, a three-line 18px paragraph whose opening phrase sits on a pale-blue highlighter block, a glossy blue gradient pill button and an 11px reassurance line. The bottom third is a huge blurred cobalt-to-cyan cloud silhouette, the logo enlarged to full width, with the top of a white app window rising from the fold and a handwritten note with a scribbled arrow at its right corner.
references.type: Lastik, a high-contrast display serif, regular weight, title case, -0.05em tracking at 92px so letters nearly touch; reused at 28-40px for section and card titles. Open Runde, a rounded Inter variant, for body at 15-18px and all UI. About a 5x jump.
references.colour: #fcfdff #0b1f33 #0077fe #eaf5fb #22c4ff #e5e8ea — White and very pale blue with deep navy text and one electric blue for the button and the cloud glow, which shades to cyan at its edges. Sections never change ground. Cool.
references.imagery: Light-mode app screenshots, large, with edges and lower halves dissolving into the page; cropped UI fragments inside cards with one element sharpened and lifted. Soft cloud and sky washes behind sections.
references.layout: 1230px container, centred hero, then a repeating module of heading, short copy and a large faded screenshot. One three-card row. Soft blue cloud washes replace hard section breaks; about twelve screens.

sections.description: Centred pill eyebrow and two-line serif heading, a short centred paragraph, then three equal cards (about 400px wide, 1px pale border, 12px radius, faint blue glow at the top). Each card's upper 55% is a cropped, softened fragment of product UI with one sharp element popped forward (a blue chip, a figure, a tooltip); below, a serif card title and three lines of centred grey text.

Repeated feature row: a two-line serif heading at about 28px on the left whose second line is a paler slate-blue, a two-line paragraph on the right starting at the 55% mark, then a full-width app screenshot whose sides and lower part dissolve into the white page rather than sitting in a frame. Faint cloud texture drifts behind.

A three-column checklist of features with round blue tick bullets, unreleased items greyed and tagged with tiny chips, and a blue gradient pill button beneath, all over a soft photographic sky wash. The footer continues on the same wash with an app-icon tile and three link columns under serif headings.

steal: Enlarge the logo silhouette to full width, blur it heavily, and use it as the coloured stage behind the product screenshot.
Mark the opening phrase of the sub-headline with a pale highlighter block instead of bolding it.
Let product screenshots dissolve into the page at their edges rather than boxing them in a browser frame.

references.name: Dabbit
references.idea: The colour picker demonstrates itself on the page: its loupe sits in the hero reading the site's own background hex, and every feature is shown as a real fragment of the app.
references.hero: Near-black viewport split exactly in half by a one-pixel vertical hairline. Left half: a small chrome four-petal logo top-left at a 40px margin, then two thirds of empty dark, then everything else anchored bottom-left: a one-line 30px medium-weight headline, three lines of grey 18px copy, a light pill button beside an outlined pill, and a tiny note. Right half: a 450px rounded square with a thin iridescent border, the app's loupe, empty except for a centre crosshair dot and a small chip reading the hex of the page's own background. Eight pastel dots and lozenges drift across the top-right like spilled swatches.
references.type: InterVariable only. Headline a modest 30px medium with -0.025em tracking; section heads about 22px; cell titles 15px; body 16px grey. Largest text is 3.3vw. Hierarchy comes from white against grey rather than size; hex values use tabular figures.
references.colour: #141416 #2b2b2e #f4f3f2 #9a9aa0 #f4a48c #d4c6e6 — Charcoal ground, off-white and grey text, no brand accent. All colour comes from the product: pastel swatches, tonal scales, and a thin prismatic edge on the loupe and logo. Neutral-cool.
references.imagery: Live-drawn UI fragments on canvas: swatch strips, eleven-step scales, contrast tables, a Figma plugin panel, each in a slightly lighter rounded panel. A chrome 3D logo and chrome price numerals are the only non-UI images.
references.layout: 40px outer margins; the hero's centre hairline becomes a three-column then four-column hairline grid. No section changes background; rhythm is small eyebrow, heading, grid, repeat. Text sits top-left in every cell.

sections.description: A three-column grid ruled by one-pixel hairlines with no card backgrounds. Each cell is over 400px tall: 15px white title and three lines of grey copy, plus a real UI fragment docked above or below (a swatch history strip, a tonal scale, a contrast table, a ten-by-ten colour matrix). Rows alternate text-over-mock and mock-over-text so the grid staggers. The loupe square from the hero reappears floating across cell boundaries.

A four-column, three-row grid of minor features divided by hairlines. Each item is a 14px title prefixed by a tiny coloured glyph (dot, square, triangle or dash, one shape per column, in the app's pastel colours) and two lines of grey text. No icons, no cards, no hover chrome.

Left third: small grey eyebrow, a 22px heading, one paragraph. Right: the price rendered as huge chrome 3D numerals about 150px tall with the loupe square overlapping them, a tiny qualifier beside, and a plain four-line checklist beneath. No pricing card, no border, no tiers.

Closing block centred on the same dark ground: the chrome four-petal logo enlarged to about 200px, pastel shapes scattered widely around it, a two-line 22px sentence, the same two pill buttons, then a one-line footer with copyright left and seven text links right.

steal: Make the hero demo sample the page itself: the tool reports the site's own background value, proving the product without a screenshot.
Build feature grids from hairlines and real UI fragments instead of bordered cards and icons, alternating text-above and mock-above per row.
Keep the headline small (30px) and anchored bottom-left so the product object, not the slogan, owns the first viewport.
